assessmentSummary.identity: A reactive backpedal-to-sprint variant in which an unpredictable live point selects the turn side and sprint path.
currentCardFindings: The description states a coach point but does not define cue location, wait window, turn choices, angle, backward boundary, sprint distance, wrong-response rule, finish, or run-out.
A signal selecting the turn side adds perception, inhibition, decision accuracy, and supervision beyond the pre-planned task.
No exact combined legacy media exist; visible candidates separately show base turns or reactive forward-to-backward sequences.

proposedDosage.progressWhen: no guessing, balanced correct choices, clean turns, and stable sprint quality

athleteInstructions: Backpedal to the boundary, read the true point, open to that side, and sprint through the target

assessmentSummary.programmingDecision: Retain as a reactive variant of the backpedal-open-turn identity. Quarantine until the cue map, angles, distances, error rules, and an exact combined demonstration are reviewed.

currentCardSnapshot.description: The athlete waits for a live cue (coach points turn side), selects the correct answer, performs the movement response, and resets before the next rep. The rep counts only when the athlete reacts to the real stimulus rather than guessing early.
currentCardSnapshot.familyKey: Reactive Change of Direction, Braking, and Re-Acceleration

evidence.sourceTitle: Lower extremity joint kinetics and energetics during backward running
evidence.sourcePublisher: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
claims: Backward running uses lower-extremity joint kinetics and muscle roles that differ from forward running.

Backpedal-to-Sprint Turn on Signal must define backward travel distance and speed, open-turn angle and side, cue predictability, forward sprint path and distance, terminal action, and run-out. A generic turn and an open turn are the same identity when those dimensions match.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Horizontal deceleration requires coordinated reduction of momentum before a direction or velocity change.

Backpedal-to-Sprint Turn on Signal belongs to backward locomotion, reorientation, and forward re-acceleration. An unpredictable side cue is a reactive variant, while adding a required terminal stick creates a distinct braking-and-balance task.

evidence.sourceTitle: Lower extremity joint kinetics and energetics during backward running
evidence.sourcePublisher: Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise
claims: Backward running can shift propulsive and absorptive roles between the knee and ankle compared with forward running.

Represent quadriceps, gluteals, hamstrings, plantar flexors, tibialis anterior, hip rotators, abductors and adductors, trunk, and arm action across the backward steps, turn, sprint, and any terminal braking.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Direction and velocity changes require control of whole-body momentum and effective braking force orientation.

Maintain backward posture and short controlled contacts, lower the centre of mass before the turn, plant without crossing or twisting, open the hips and eyes toward the target, re-accelerate, and use additional braking steps for a stick finish.

evidence.sourceTitle: Are Change of Direction Speed and Reactive Agility Useful for Determining the Optimal Field Position for Young Soccer Players?
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
claims: Reactive movement differs from the same pre-planned path because the athlete must identify an unpredictable target before selecting the direction.

Score technical complexity, absolute-load demand, coordination, supervision, failure consequence, impact, work-capacity demand, and overall difficulty directly. Athlete experience remains programming context, not an exercise-card skill level.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Repeated braking and re-acceleration can accumulate substantial mechanical and neuromuscular demand.

Backpedal-to-Sprint Turn on Signal must track backward contacts, turns per side and angle, sprint and braking contacts, direction decisions, intensity, surface, quadriceps and plantar-flexor load, groin and hip-rotator stress, technical fatigue, recovery, and total change-of-direction volume.
Quality speed work requires a suitable surface, marked targets, spacing, run-out, and recovery.

Require a clear dry lane, visible backward boundary, turn and finish marks, safe sightline or cue source, athlete separation, and enough sprint and stopping space; cones and video are optional unless used to define the path.
Speed work should prescribe distance, intensity, repetitions, sets, and recovery.

Use two to five high-quality repetitions per turn side, roughly 2–5 metres backward plus 5–15 metres forward, with 60–180 seconds recovery; reduce intent and distance during learning or terminal-stick preparation.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Braking and direction change quality depend on controlling momentum and aligning the body for the next task.

Backpedal under control, keep the turn boundary visible, lower before the plant, open through the hip without crossing the feet, find the sprint target, accelerate through it, and use the assigned run-out or stick zone.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Resistance Training: Updated Position Statement Paper From the NSCA
claims: Training should use appropriate supervision, correct technique, manageable demands, and gradual progression.

Stop for pain, backward trip, heel catch, crossed feet, uncontrolled trunk rotation, knee collapse, slip, wrong direction, lane conflict, unsafe braking, repeated anticipation, marked speed loss, or inability to see or use the finish zone.
High-quality acceleration work should be placed before fatigue and not converted into conditioning by excessive density.

Backpedal-to-Sprint Turn on Signal fits movement intelligence or output after backward-locomotion and braking preparation. Teach the pre-planned turn before reactive side choice and add a terminal stick only when the athlete can brake safely.
Acceleration develops across successive steps rather than through immediate upright running.

Show the backward stance, line of sight, both turn sides and angles, plant and open-turn sequence, first three forward contacts, sprint target, run-out, and any stick zone from front, side, and rear views.

evidence.sourceTitle: Biomechanical and Neuromuscular Performance Requirements of Horizontal Deceleration: A Review with Implications for Random Intermittent Multi-Directional Sports
claims: Deceleration assessment should account for approach velocity, braking strategy, body position, and task constraints.

Provide backward and forward distance marks, turn-angle and side balance, cue schedule, rear and side observation, plant-foot and trunk checks, sprint and braking contact counts, error rules, speed-loss stops, and exact alias or variant decisions.

evidence.sourceTitle: Youth Training and Long-Term Athletic Development
claims: Movement training should be developmentally appropriate and based on competency.

Accessibility options include walking backward, fewer backward steps, a pre-planned side, 90-degree rather than 180-degree turn, slower sprint, wider lane, visual boundary, no timing, longer run-out, no terminal stick, extra demonstration, and longer recovery.

evidence.sourceTitle: Are Change of Direction Speed and Reactive Agility Useful for Determining the Optimal Field Position for Young Soccer Players?
evidence.sourcePublisher: Journal of Sports Science and Medicine
claims: Pre-planned and reactive versions may share a movement path while differing in whether the target direction is known.

Turn and open turn are naming aliases when angle and side rules match; a live side signal is a reactive variant, while a terminal stick, repeated shuttle, lateral break, or sprint-to-backpedal reversal changes the task.
YouTube supports privacy-enhanced embedding through youtube-nocookie.com.

Visible links for Backpedal-to-Sprint Turn on Signal remain candidate-only. Availability, embedding, exact backward distance, turn angle and side, cue, sprint path, terminal action, complete viewing, captions, safety, reviewer identity, and approval are separate gates.
